g.text: Two separate bracket expressions evaluated in turn, combined with precedence-driven reduction
Push initial tokens and evaluate first bracket: '2', '+', '(', '8', '-', '2', ')'
• Push 2 to operand stack, push '+' to operator stack: [+]
• Push '(', then 8, then '-' (sees '(' on top, so pushes directly), then 2
Push 6. Pop matching '(' and discard. Stack state: operand [2, 6], operator [+]
The first bracket is completely evaluated to 6 and removed!
Process '/', push '3', then '*' triggers equal-priority evaluation '6 / 3 = 2'
Push 2. Now compare '*' with new top '+' (2 > 1) → Push '*'!
Operator stack now holds: [+, *]. Operand stack holds: [2, 2].
Left-to-right rule: '*' waited while '/' evaluated first.
• Push '(', then 6, then '+' (sees '(' on top, pushed directly), then 2
Push 8. Pop matching '(' and discard. Stack state: operand [2, 2, 8], operator [+, *]
Second bracket resolved to 8. Expression reduced to: 2 + 2 * 8
End of string reached! Ready for final flushing of remaining operators.
End of String: Flush Remaining Operators '*' then '+' → Final Result 18
String ended. Flush remaining operator stack in LIFO order:
Push 16. Operator stack top is now '+'. Operand stack: [2, 16]
Push 18. Operator stack is empty → STOP!
while (ostack.size() > 0 && ostack.peek() != '(' && prec(ostack.peek()) >= prec(ch)) { pop op, v2, v1; push operation(v1, v2, op); }
